title: THE RIVER THAT COULD NOT SAVE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The fish in the Nile will die, and the river will stink; the Egyptians will not be able to drink its water.'" Then the Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over the streams and canals, over the ponds and all the reservoirs'—and they will turn to blood. Blood will be everywhere in Egypt, even in vessels of wood and stone."" - Exodus 7:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God targets the Nile with precision. Egypt's agriculture, trade, drinking water, and religion all flowed from this river. It was worshipped as a giver of life.

Now it gives death. The fish die. The water stinks. Nothing is drinkable.

There is a grim justice in this. The river Pharaoh once filled with Hebrew babies now runs red. What was used for cruelty becomes the site of judgement.

The deeper lesson is about idols. An idol is anything we trust to give us life. And every idol has the same limitation: it can be taken away, and it cannot save us when it goes.

Egypt's god was reduced to something they could not even drink. That is what happens eventually to everything we put in God's place — it fails at the exact point where we needed it most.

Jesus stood up and offered something different: whoever drinks the water I give will never thirst again (Jn 4:14). Only one source of life cannot be turned to blood.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What would collapse in my life if it were taken away tomorrow?
2. Am I drinking from Christ, or from something that will eventually fail me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone are the source of life. Loosen my grip on things that cannot save and satisfy me in Yourself. Amen.
